messages:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: PAGER: model-loader errors in us-west-2 (svc-models). Error spike at 03:02 UTC -> >5% 5xx for large-model routes. Paging on-call.

Samir G: I’m on-call, taking this. Any immediate customer-facing mitigation suggestions?

Tara R: seeing a bunch of compile-timeout traces and some deserialization errors during warmup. Logs: 
```
E 03:01:57 model-loader model_id=gpt-xx-large warmup: compile kernel timed out after 10000ms (nvrtc)
E 03:02:01 model-loader model_id=gpt-xx-large warmup: deserialization failed: unexpected EOF
E 03:02:10 runtime: oom while allocating KV cache for seq_len=8192
```

Jessie K: this looks like two failure modes stacking: (1) nvrtc/native TLS/JIT kernels occasionally hang/timeout at compile for very large models, (2) when compile fails we fall back into an attempted deserialize path which sometimes OOMs for the large seq lengths. Both cause the init to fail and the container to crash.

Lee M: Customer-impact: Support dashboard shows errors from 3 paying tenants (ids: T-108, T-212, T-391) and a rising error rate for long-context routes (>4096). We should mark incidents for those tenants and open support tickets.

Samir G: Immediate plan: 1) Stop warmup compile on new loads for affected model variant, 2) divert traffic to a compatible smaller/quantized variant, 3) increase compile timeout as short-term.

Jessie K: Agree. Rolling actions now:
- patch control-plane to set model_compile_timeout_ms=60000 for svc-models in us-west-2
- set env MODEL_JIT=0 for the loader pods for variant gpt-xx-large- fp16
- update routing to send 100% of gpt-xx-large traffic to gpt-xx-large-quant-v1 (smaller memory)

OpsBot: Action triggered: set model_compile_timeout_ms=60000 for pool=us-west-2-svc-models by Samir G.

Samir G: Applying routing change: `POST /internal/routing` -> shifting traffic to quant-v1 in us-west-2.

Tara R: Restarting model-loader pods one at a time to pick up env change. Using rolling restart to avoid mass fail. Command: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/model-loader -n svc-models --field-selector=spec.nodeName!=gpu-node-7`

Jessie K: Also disabling warmup compile for new loads: patch config: 
```
curl -s -X POST https://control-plane.internal/api/v1/config 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' 
  -d '{"model_compile_timeout_ms":60000, "jit_enabled":false, "warmup_enabled":true, "warmup_compile":false}'
```
(ops validated)

Lee M: Support note drafted: "We’re seeing transient model warmup failures for large-context models in us-west-2 causing 5xx for a small subset of requests. Traffic has been routed to a lower-memory quantized variant while we investigate. Impacted customers have been notified."

Samir G: After changes, error rate dropped from 5.6% -> 0.8% for the route. Some nodes still show loader restarts but no new compile-timeout errors.

Jessie K: Root cause hypothesis: a new compiler kernel change combined with larger-than-expected compile queue depth leads to nvrtc timeout. When kernel compile fails the loader attempts deserialization path which increases peak memory and causes OOM during kv cache allocation.

Tara R: Next steps:
- Jess to reproduce locally with env to force nvrtc stalling and capture core dumps (ACTION: Jessie K)
- Infra to add backoff/queue limits to compile threadpool (ACTION: Samir G)
- Product to decide whether to roll model variant pin globally (ACTION: Lee M)

Jessie K: I’ll open a tracking ticket with reproducer, logs, and suggested code changes. Putting a temporary alert to auto-fallback to quantized variant on >3 compile timeouts in 5m.

Samir G: Handoff: I’ll stay for the follow-up and patch, Jess will own the postmortem and remediation. If anything regresses, ping me and we’ll re-route traffic region-wide.

Lee M: Noted. I’ve contacted reps for the three tenants; they acknowledged the workaround.

IncidentBot: Status update posted to status.redwood.ai/incidents/2112234567. Severity: High -> Customers informed.

Samir G: Closing pager for now; monitoring 30m. Will reopen if >1% error for tenant-critical routes. :thumbsup:

Jessie K: Assigned postmortem to `ENG-ML#4572`. Will include timeline, reproducer, and long-term fix (queue backpressure + safer deserialize fallback).

Tara R: Thanks all. Good rapid coordination.

Samir G: +1 — closing thread (monitoring).
